meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided to give my son a zero, and when?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me about the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. He writes somewhere else and pastes it in when it's done.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record. And it stays between us, not in front of his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time. A bad quotation costs marks, Hale, not the whole essay.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
What exactly are you proposing, then? Whatever it is, nothing goes in his file, and I'll want that in writing.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. That's what an outline is for.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything wrong. Private, after school, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check his shifts at the store tonight. Put Thursday in your email, and I'll confirm by reply.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school, not in front of Owen's class and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record, and you proposed Thursday the twelfth. I still require that promise in writing, including that nothing goes on his record, and I will confirm Thursday once I have checked Owen's shifts. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him; she still wants your written promise tonight that nothing goes on his record, and she still has to confirm Thursday; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: When she claimed Owen wrote the essay elsewhere and pasted it in, you invited him to bring that draft with its date, so the version history stood, because it was dated, checkable and tied to his own work.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero going in before the call home, you led with documents rather than the detector score, and you never called Owen a liar.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on a late October night, very close to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their minds between an outline and an essay, answer that point directly, for example by saying the rewrite will let Owen explain how his argument changed, before you move on to the offer.
